stages.title: Foundations: integrated care and needs assessment
stages.summary: Two linked projects start here. iCARE-PD (Integrated Parkinson Care Networks) is a multinational research consortium, funded in 2018 by the EU Joint Programme on Neurodegenerative Disease Research (JPND) and CIHR, that co-designs an integrated care model: health and social care organised around the person at home and in the community, with a PD nurse as the single point of contact. eCARE-PD is born inside this project (first called the 'PD virtual coach'): a digital companion that helps people living with Parkinson's choose care priorities, track them, receive tailored care tips and share what they observe with their care team. A needs study with people living with Parkinson's, caregivers and health professionals (2017–2018) and a systematic review of mHealth acceptability set the ground for both.
stages.methods_data: Needs and expectations study (2017–2018); qualitative systematic review of mHealth for PD self-management.
stages.key_outputs: Grant awarded; review identifies technological, social and financial factors of acceptability; exploratory low-fidelity prototype.

stages.title: Iteration 1 — eCARE-PD 1.0: list of PD symptoms
stages.summary: First co-design cycle of eCARE-PD in four phases (preparation, mapping, test & use, final solution): eCARE-PD emerges as a 'digital companion' for self-care. In parallel, iCARE-PD's narrative interviews in five countries (Oct 2019–Aug 2020) collect the stories that become three patient trajectories (see the iCARE-PD column 2021–2022).
stages.methods_data: Participatory design workshops (mapping, N=21); 3-week home test of β prototype (N=30); remote design critique sessions (N=21).
stages.participants: Mapping 21 (10 PwP, 6 caregivers, 3 nurses, 2 neurologists); home test 30; final solution 21
stages.key_outputs: Six key design features; six usage issues; three design requirements; adaptive + adaptable tailoring.

stages.title: Iteration 2 — eCARE-PD 2.0: three main categories, designed and tested at home
stages.summary: Findings from iteration 1 shape eCARE-PD 2.0, a web-based patient portal that organises care priorities in three clinical categories and adds symptom tracking, care tips and resources, a diary, wearables and a Care Finder for local resources, echoing the community resources asked for in the iCARE-PD workshops. With Parkinson Canada funding the digital self-management app (2023), the portal is then put to the test: from December 2023, people living with Parkinson's use it at home for 8 weeks. In daily life the three categories reach their limits: prioritizing is hard, tips feel generic, and users ask for support to set their own goals.
stages.methods_data: Integration of the iteration-1 design requirements and development of the web portal (2021–2023), then a usage diary study at home (Dec 2023–Jun 2024): weekly diaries and semi-structured interviews (45–75 min), with CTI-Lab focus groups (3 patient/caregiver groups, 1 provider group).
stages.participants: Home test: 20 enrolled (F=10/M=10, 55–79 y, EN=16/FR=4); 18 diaries; 18 interviews
stages.key_outputs: eCARE-PD 2.0 interface (care priorities in 3 categories, tracking surveys, care tips & resources library, diary, dashboard, Care Finder, Fitbit integration); from the home test: usage triggers, user profiles (anxious, selective, episodic, diligent), barriers and design requirements (Table 2).

stages.title: Iteration 3 — eCARE-PD 3.0: translating analysis into design
stages.summary: Design team holds 20 collective working sessions to revise the taxonomy and design the CAFY dialogue flow. PD-TIPS.AI is funded by CIHR.
stages.methods_data: 20 collective working sessions: 7 (Nov '24–Feb '25) usage-study analysis; 3 (Mar–Apr '25) taxonomy revision; 4 (May '25) CAFY dialogue flow; 3 (Jun–Jul '25) consolidation; 2 (Sep '25) probe finalization.
stages.participants: Design team N=8 (neurologists, research assistants, researchers)
stages.key_outputs: Taxonomy: domains & sub-domains organised by 5 main topics; CAFY design probe; care-tips typology (v11.2025). First CAFY prototype (Mar 2025); task-oriented CAFY assistant (May 2025); new visual identity and structure redesign; eCARE-PD prototype with a first complete CAFY user flow (Jun–Dec 2025).

stages.title: Iteration 4 — Participatory design workshops: testing CAFY and sorting the taxonomy
stages.summary: People living with Parkinson's and caregivers use the CAFY probe and sort taxonomy cards. Three tensions surface: symptom vs lived experience, description vs intention to act, fixed categories vs boundary zones.
stages.methods_data: Activity 1: CAFY dialogue testing (think-aloud); Activity 2: card sorting. Reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke).
stages.participants: N=26 across three groups (G1, G2, G3)

stages.title: Iteration 5 — Participatory design workshops: actionable care tips and self-care data visualisation
stages.summary: People living with Parkinson's and caregivers evaluate the actionability of self-care tips tailored to different patient personas and self-care data visualizations.
stages.methods_data: Patient workshops on care-tip actionability and data visualisation (Apr 2026); CTI-Lab 'Journey' page ideation session (Jun 2026).
stages.key_outputs: Low-fidelity prototype of data visualisation ('Journey' page, Jul 2026).

stages.title: Iteration 6 — Intentions, not symptoms; taxonomy as infrastructure
stages.summary: The taxonomy is rebuilt around five first-person intentions (entry points into CAFY), with domains/sub-domains and cross-cutting tags, then inscribed as the data model of the conversational recommender system (CRS v1.0).
stages.methods_data: CTI-Lab session of 9 March 2026. Conceptual analysis (reflective journal, conceptual memos); online interviews for personas and usage scenarios (Jun–Aug 2026).
stages.key_outputs: Three-level taxonomy (intentions → domains/sub-domains → tags); CRS data model IntentDomain → SubDomain → Term → CareTip → Resource. e-Care PD full-workflow demo with care-tips logic engine (Sep 2026).

stages.title: iCARE-PD — From patients' trajectories to an integrated care network
stages.summary: Running alongside eCARE-PD, the iCARE-PD consortium turns the stories of 94 people living with Parkinson's in five countries into three illness trajectories: unpredictable, situated and demanding. Each trajectory has its own care priorities. In Canada, people living with Parkinson's, care partners and professionals then map today's fragmented 'web of care' and co-design the integrated care network that should support them: personal, care and community networks connected around a single point of contact, the PD nurse. Digital tools such as eCARE-PD are part of this network.
stages.methods_data: Narrative interviews (Oct 2019–Aug 2020) analysed with Corbin & Strauss's trajectory framework; remote design-scenario workshops in Canada (Jun–Oct 2021): journey mapping and inspiration cards, analysed with actor-network theory; co-design testing of sensor technologies (MooVeo) in five tertiary centres (2021–2022).
stages.participants: Narrative interviews 94 (Canada, Czech Republic, Germany, Spain, Ireland); Canadian workshops 15 (10 PwP + 5 HCP); MooVeo 31
stages.key_outputs: Three illness trajectories; care delivery priorities and network components for each trajectory; journey map for Canada; roadmap and toolkit for the Canadian care network; sensor co-design method.

stages.title: iCARE-PD — Multinational results, and trajectories carried into PD-TIPS.AI
stages.summary: The integrated care model was tested in six countries as a 4-month program led by a trained iCARE-PD nurse (May 2021–Feb 2023, N=202). The results, published in 2026, show high completion (96.5%) and a better perceived quality of chronic care. The patient trajectories developed in iCARE-PD are a foundational aspect of the patient personas built in PD-TIPS.AI: integrated care research feeds the design of the AI conversational recommender.
stages.methods_data: Multinational prospective pre-post study in six PD tertiary centres (Canada, Czechia, France, Germany, Ireland, Portugal): individualized care plans, system navigation and self-care support.
stages.participants: 202 enrolled (newly diagnosed 43, intermediate 54, complex care needs 105)
stages.key_outputs: Care integration shown to be transferable across health systems; agile toolkit in development; trajectories reused as a basis for PD-TIPS.AI personas.

quotes.quote: Of course, uncertainty is also part of the problem. What is it going to happen? I don't know. How will things go? I do not know.
Okay, well I can tell you that I was not geared or pointed towards any community services or any information of any kind for Parkinson's.
By using the tracking, I realized I had pain (tightness) every day and did not realize before how much tightness.
But what matters most to you? This really isn't the top priority… if we just focused on two today, does that make sense?

but these personal insights is the one that just strikes me as the most interesting and the most useful because it's like, bang, here's things that you need to do to make your life better. And not only that, it's not just like, hey, why don't you exercise? You'll have less muscle stiffness. You have less fatigue. Like you actually are experiencing better results. And that's pretty powerful. Because I can tell you, go exercise. And you're like, yeah, leave me alone. But then you've reported, without even thinking about it, that on the day you exercised, you felt better. And then here's the evidence. And it's not me telling you. It's you telling yourself

I'm not a numbers person, so I don't tend to look at the percentages per se, although it helps to see green or red. But it was the description of the link between my activity and my symptom. So for example, if I see less water, more fatigue, oh. I might try to increase my water. I do five out of seven days to do whatever I'm going to try to improve that.

integrated_care.title: iCARE-PD: Integrated Parkinson Care Networks
integrated_care.narrative: A multinational consortium funded through the EU Joint Programme on Neurodegenerative Disease Research (JPND) and CIHR sets out to build a sustainable care model for people living with Parkinson's: a shift from (in)outpatient care to a home- and community-based model centred on care integration, self-management support and technology-enabled care. Co-design is the method: the experience of patients and care partners is built into the design of the care model, in four linked steps.
integrated_care.key_points:
Step 1: prepare and set up the study
Step 2: capture patients' stories and understand their illness trajectories
Step 3: design scenarios for an integrated care network with patients, care partners and health professionals
Step 4: co-produce solutions to implement a tailored integrated care network in each country
integrated_care.countries: Canada; Czech Republic; France; Germany; Ireland; Spain
integrated_care.link_to_ecarepd: eCARE-PD starts inside this project: the digital companion is one of the technologies meant to support self-management at home.

integrated_care.title: Narrative interviews in five countries: three illness trajectories
integrated_care.narrative: 94 people living with Parkinson's and their care partners tell the story of life with the disease. Analysed with Corbin and Strauss's illness-trajectory framework, the stories reveal three typical trajectories. Each is shaped by the work of patients (self-care), care partners (informal care) and health professionals (formal care). The illness trajectory is neither stable nor linear: it depends on medical conditions but also on social and personal ones, such as access to community services or financial resources. The Canadian analysis draws the same three trajectories as 'unpredictable', 'oscillating' and 'burning' (figure).
integrated_care.key_points:
Unpredictable: newly diagnosed people (2 years or less); uncertainty, stigma, the emotional impact of the diagnosis, experienced as a life disruption
Situated: many care pathways that depend on each person's medical and social situation; adapting to fluctuations and changing daily life
Demanding: symptoms poorly controlled or evolving quickly, crisis episodes, vulnerable people (comorbidities, low income); a growing burden on the care partner
integrated_care.participants: 94 (Canada 19, Czech Republic 20, Germany 21, Spain 16, Ireland 19); mostly patient and care-partner dyads
integrated_care.countries: Canada; Czech Republic; Germany; Spain; Ireland
integrated_care.image_caption: Typical trajectories for people living with PD in Canada (Sendra, Grosjean & Bonneville, 2022, Fig. 3).
integrated_care.link_to_ecarepd: Trajectory mapping is also the starting point of the eCARE-PD 1.0 workshops in the same iteration.

integrated_care.title: From trajectories to the components of an integrated care network
integrated_care.narrative: For each trajectory, people describe the work they do at home (illness-related, everyday-life and biographical work) and the care they need to carry it out. Each trajectory calls for its own care delivery priorities and its own components of an integrated care network. These components become hypotheses to discuss, negotiate and rearrange in the participatory design workshops of the next step.
integrated_care.key_points:
Unpredictable: personalized care; tailored, reliable information about PD; access to the specialized team; support groups; emotional and psychological support. Components: a single point of contact from diagnosis, a co-produced roadmap, a resource kit for newly diagnosed people
Situated: care navigation and community linkages; bundled information on social care; tailored programs; efficient communication with care teams; joint assessment to anticipate needs. Components: a nurse coordinator, a map of local services, self-tracking and telemonitoring tools
Demanding: support and advice for care partners; access to social benefits, in-home services and transportation; proactive monitoring to prevent complications. Components: a resource kit for care partners, a help line during acute phases, home-based monitoring (e.g. ON/OFF states)
integrated_care.countries: Canada; Czech Republic; Germany; Spain; Ireland
integrated_care.image_caption: Main care delivery priorities and components of an integrated care network for each trajectory (Grosjean et al., 2021, Fig. 2).
integrated_care.link_to_ecarepd: Digital health technologies for self-management (self-tracking, telemonitoring, educational resources) are one of the components: this is the place eCARE-PD takes in the network.

integrated_care.title: Design-scenario workshops in Canada: the current care network, mapped
integrated_care.narrative: Held remotely because of COVID-19, workshops with people living with Parkinson's, care partners and health professionals map the journey from diagnosis to daily life: key events, touchpoints, feelings, barriers and facilitators. The journey map shows a care network that is fragmented and medically oriented. People must connect the actors of a 'web of care' themselves, and their social needs are overlooked.
integrated_care.key_points:
Seven events: diagnostic process; stopping work or activities; treatment plan; symptoms in daily life; disease progression; changes at home, mobility and transport; hospitalisation and rehabilitation
The experience is most negative at diagnosis, during ON/OFF episodes and communication challenges, and when stronger symptoms require home care and medical equipment
Personal, care and community networks are enrolled over time but are not always connected to each other
Everyone wishes for a single point of contact to guide them as the disease evolves; patient organisations are active and valued
integrated_care.participants: 15: 10 people living with PD (3 with a care partner) and 5 health professionals (3 neurologists, 1 PD nurse, 1 physiotherapist)
integrated_care.image_caption: Journey map for Canada: touchpoints, experience, barriers and facilitators at seven key events (Gauthier-Beaupré et al., 2022, Fig. 2).

integrated_care.title: An integrated care network: three connected networks around a single point of contact
integrated_care.narrative: In the second workshop activity, participants imagine an integrated care network based on home and community care. Read through actor-network theory, their scenarios connect three networks (personal, care and community) around a single point of contact, with mediators and shared tools that hold the network together. The network has to be made and remade over time to follow each person's trajectory. The study ends with a roadmap and toolkit for setting up iCARE-PD in Canada.
integrated_care.key_points:
A single point of contact and navigation tools, with the specialized PD nurse as the focal actor
Intermediaries: PD nurse, patient buddy, family orientation program, patient advisory board, electronic health record, eConsult and help line
Information brokers chosen with each person: family doctor, social worker or allied health professional
Shared tools: assessment tools, tailored educational resources, emotional and psychological programs, sensors and wearable devices
Requirement: a network that is personalized and malleable as needs change over time
integrated_care.participants: Same 15 participants (10 people living with PD, 5 health professionals)
integrated_care.link_to_ecarepd: The roadmap and toolkit are outputs of Iteration 2, alongside eCARE-PD 2.0 and its Care Finder for local resources.

integrated_care.title: The iCARE-PD program in six countries
integrated_care.narrative: The co-designed model is put into practice as a 4-month program led by a trained iCARE-PD nurse, who acts as a clinical care integrator, in six Parkinson's tertiary centres in Europe and Canada. Participants are enrolled in three groups according to their expected care needs: newly diagnosed, intermediate, and complex care needs.
integrated_care.key_points:
Initial visit: care priorities and goals set with the nurse through shared decision-making (the 5A's: Assess, Advise, Agree, Assist, Arrange)
A personalized care plan, shared with the family doctor and the PD specialist
A follow-up call at 1 month and a close-out visit at 4 months
Each site maps its regional PD care network and builds a resource database for quick referrals
Nurses complete a 6-month competency training in care integration
integrated_care.participants: 529 screened; 202 enrolled: newly diagnosed 43, intermediate 54, complex care needs 105
integrated_care.countries: Canada (Ottawa); Czechia (Prague); France (Toulouse); Germany (Marburg); Ireland (Dublin); Portugal (Torres Vedras)
integrated_care.link_to_ecarepd: Choosing care priorities and turning them into goals with a nurse is the gesture that eCARE-PD and CAFY later support at home.

integrated_care.title: Care integration travels across health systems
integrated_care.narrative: The program was implemented across very different social, cultural and health-care contexts, during the COVID-19 pandemic, with high completion rates and a better perception of chronic care. The authors present the health outcomes as encouraging but preliminary (pre-post design without a control group) and call for a multinational cluster randomized trial. An agile toolkit is being developed to deploy iCARE-PD in real life. Published online in 2025, in the February 2026 issue of Movement Disorders.
integrated_care.key_points:
Median site enrollment 69.6% (range 21.1–100); program completion 96.5%
Perceived quality of chronic illness care improved (PACIC+ total +0.48, 95% CI 0.34–0.61), most for goal setting (+0.60)
Improvement in non-tremor motor scores in the complex-care-needs group
Most frequent care priorities: mobility, balance and falls (37.1%), exercise and hobbies (28.2%), sleep (23.8%), speech and communication (21.3%), anxiety (19.3%)
'Knowledge about treatment' was a priority mainly for newly diagnosed people (32.6%)
integrated_care.countries: Canada; Czechia; France; Germany; Ireland; Portugal
integrated_care.link_to_ecarepd: The most frequent care priorities (mobility, sleep, communication, anxiety) are the kind of items people select in eCARE-PD's care-priority taxonomy.

integrated_care.title: From illness trajectories to patient personas
integrated_care.narrative: The three illness trajectories identified in iCARE-PD (unpredictable, situated, demanding) are a foundation of the patient personas developed in PD-TIPS.AI. Built from online interviews with people living with Parkinson's (June–August 2026), the personas and usage scenarios help design a conversational recommender that responds to people at different points of their journey, not only to a list of symptoms.
integrated_care.key_points:
Trajectories give each persona a moment in the illness journey: newly diagnosed and uncertain, adapting to fluctuations, or facing a demanding phase with a care partner
Personas and usage scenarios are used to design and test the PD-TIPS.AI conversational recommender

intro_quotes.quote: When I go to the clinic, you're just given a sheet saying this is the symptoms. Like there's no place to direct you, and you have to do your homework on your own.

intro_quotes.speaker_detail: Labelled P2 in the paper (speaks as a clinician)
intro_quotes.quote: If ideally, we could have technology that could help us to understand what's happening to people living with Parkinson's between clinical visits, that would be huge, but […] I don't think you're interested in getting the big data, 20 pages of a report, but in an eloquent, synthetic way a portrait of how, a snapshot of how the patient has been doing in the six months prior to seeing them in person.

I was looking for nuggets of learnings and the only nugget I felt I got was the tracking of my symptoms over time. Like which symptoms were variable and which might come next for my attention, things like that.
